analysis: Examined the two head-text units of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift (lines 2231-3069), a UI/orchestration layer for `darkbloom cluster` onboarding. Changes relevant to security: new ClusterOnboardingOperations hooks `stopsAsked` (default nil) and `serveUnlessStopped` (default nil, falls back to `serve`) at ~1518-1525; `provision(...)` gains a `stopsBefore` argument; chooseAndServe (2901-2999) now counts stops at start (`begin`), checks them before `startBothMacs` (2994-3004), and ends via `stoppedEnding` if a stop was asked. This is availability/lifecycle logic: it makes a user-requested stop win over a concurrent start, and the leading Mac re-checks under its lock (`serveUnlessStopped`). Fail-closed behavior is preserved: if the count is unreadable (nil), `stopsBefore` is re-read at 2984 and the old `serve()` fallback is used only when the live hook is unset (older build). No change to encryption, attestation, authorization, key handling, or the coordinator WebSocket contract was observed. Local-network/sudo paths (setUpPortWithSudo, runAsAdministrator) are pre-existing and unchanged in the visible hunks; TB-014's root GPU-limit path is not touched in the visible lines. Remaining questions for integration: the actual implementations of `stopsAsked`/`serveUnlessStopped` (ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked, the leading Mac lock, and the cross-Mac status reading) are outside the supplied units, so correctness of the TOCTOU guarantee (stop vs start race) and whether a peer can spoof the stop count over the cable cannot be verified here. The patch excerpt is truncated, and `provision` and `followStart` changes (beyond line 3069) were not visible. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
